newsitem.title: UK: UK's Major says Labour party would raise taxes.
newsitem.headline: UK's Major says Labour party would raise taxes.

text.p: Prime Minister John Major on Thursday renewed his charge that the main opposition Labour Party would soon raise taxes if it won next Thursday's British election.

At his daily campaign news conference, Major said Labour economics spokesman Gordon Brown was already committed to an emergency budget in July to impose a windfall tax on privatised utilities and to start plugging what Mayor said was a 12 billion pound "black hole" in his spending plans.
"Let me repeat: the only reason Labour need a budget in July is to put taxes up," Major said.
He said the windfall tax would put up the cost of making a telephone call or heating a house. It would hit pensioners and cut the value of shares held by millions of savers, Major added.
"But that is just for starters. Mr Brown would need more money to keep the specific commitments Labour have made for the first two years of their programme," Mayor said.
